sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The seanachie, or storyteller, was an important figure in rural Ireland until the late 20th century. He was a modern form of the ancient bard. The bard memorized the history and myth of the people. The seanachie told tales drawn from that same material, though the stories had degraded with time and distance. He carried the memory of the community through his yarns. His role faded as rural life changed, but the stories he kept alive shaped later Irish folklore.

okr.objective: Document the seanachie, the Irish storyteller.
